newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - July 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - July 15.

text.p: The Washington Post included the following stories on its front page on July 15:

WASHINGTON - The U.S. Census Bureau said limited use of scientific sampling is necessary to make the 2000 census accurate, a position that angers congressional Republicans who want an old-fashioned head count.
WASHINGTON - Washington's air reached unhealthful levels of ozone pollution for the second say in a row, and forecasters expected more the same on Tuesday.

RICHMOND, VIRGINIA - The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency has launched an investigation of Virginia's Department of Environmental Quality, saying the state has failed to enforce national clean air and water laws.
WASHINGTON - U.S. AIDS deaths fell by 19 percent during the first nine months of 1996, indicating that the decline in deaths from the epidemic has accelerated, federal officials said.
NEW YORK - The federal murder and racketeering trial of Vincent "Chin" Gigante, an alleged mob boss, has served up a parade of unsavory characters.

TOKYO - Since taking office early last year, Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto has combined shrewd political moves at home, a high profile abroad and a few lucky breaks to become Japan's most powerful and effective premier in a decade.
